title: ACA s. 17 — Reference by parties to arbitrator

content.overview: Section 17 confers on the arbitral tribunal the power to grant interim measures during arbitral proceedings, subject to the statutory framework.
content.glance: Section 17 confers on the arbitral tribunal the power to grant interim measures during arbitral proceedings, subject to the statutory framework.
content.study:
Module 1: Tribunal power
The tribunal may grant the classes of interim protection specified by section 17(1), including preservation, custody, inspection and other protective measures.

Module 2: Enforceability
An order under section 17(1) is enforceable in the same manner as if it were an order of the court, subject to the statutory scheme.

Module 3: Practice
After constitution of the tribunal, the section 17 remedy is central to interim protection; section 9 remains relevant within its own statutory limits.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: A party invokes section 17 for relief outside the statutory categories or ignores the requirement that the tribunal be competent to act.

hypotheticals.question: What is section 17's core function?
hypotheticals.analysis: It gives the arbitral tribunal statutory authority to grant interim measures during arbitration and gives the resulting order the enforcement status prescribed by the Act.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 17 as self-contained without reading its statutory conditions.
misconceptions.correction: Apply section 17 with the Act's express conditions and connected provisions.
